claim: Strong, significant predictive skill for volatility (corr 0.695 vs HAR 0.555, 18/18 CIs clear of zero) but none for direction (AUC 0.51-0.53, 0/18 above breakeven at 0.8 pip); no trading PnL computed, so no trading edge.
reasons: Holds: there is no trading edge. The notebook computes no PnL, direction AUC averages 0.514 over 108 folds, and no pair clears the breakeven hit rate. It is a forex study at 1h and says nothing about MNQ. MNQ costs ($2.78 = 1.39 points round trip) were never applied.

Holds: the causality and persistence numbers check out. Features at bar t use bar t and earlier. The target is next-bar log(high-low), lr.shift(-1) (git show ae0f3d0:src/forexmodel/features.py:115). Folds are expanding walk-forward with a 240-bar purge on a 1-bar target (split.py:49-79). I recomputed EURUSD 1h persistence from the lake (bars, 1m to 1h time_bucket) and it matches results/01 per fold: 0.5794/0.5955/0.6174/0.6493/0.6061/0.6173 vs CSV 0.5794/0.5963/0.6175/0.6498/0.6061/0.6181, with identical n (4006/4012).

Weak baseline, which inflates the headline: the 18/18 win over HAR is mostly hour-of-day seasonality, and the HAR used here leaves that out (lr_0/lr_5/lr_22 of the raw hourly range, baselines.py:35-41). A causal 24-value hour-of-day mean of next-bar log range, fit only on pre-fold data, scores 0.667/0.698/0.672/0.680/0.722/0.716 (mean 0.6925) on EURUSD. That is almost exactly gbr_clock_only and well above HAR's 0.6094.

Corrected lift, EURUSD: a deseasonalised HAR has 25 parameters (hour profile plus one slope on the averaged hour-residual of lags 1, 5 and 22), all fit on pre-fold data minus 240h. It scores 0.7268/0.7422/0.7520/0.7779/0.7556/0.7667, mean 0.7535. gbr_full scores 0.7640. The real incremental skill is about +0.010 per fold, positive on all 6 folds. The notebook's figure is +0.155 over HAR.

The ablation says the same thing across all 18 pairs (results/02). only_har_cascade GBR gives 0.5550, equal to har_rv. Removing intraday_season drops the model to 0.5853, only +0.030 above HAR. The ablation row the claim cites (returns -0.0005) is right, but the lift is seasonality, not model skill.

Pooled bootstrap CIs mix levels across folds. The target is a raw quote-unit log range whose level drifts across years, so pooled correlation over 6 concatenated folds rewards tracking the level. That is why clock_vs_har flips sign on 12 of 18 pairs. The 18/18 full_vs_har CIs are pooled figures, and they overstate the per-fold result. The block-240 bootstrap does correctly handle the overlap from autocorrelation.

The results are stale against the current code and cannot be rerun from HEAD. The manifest shows max_iter=300 with max_train_rows=250000 and purge 240. Current code uses a standardized target, early stopping at 5000 iterations and purge 306. The committed run_analysis.py writes a manifest different from the one on disk.

The learning curve is partly invalid by the notebook's own rule. The rows at 1,000,000 and 1,514,040 rows have iters_run=300=max_iter, so those fits hit the iteration ceiling. The CSV has no 'converged' column, so the notebook's check silently skipped them. The +0.0068 flatness claim rests on those capped fits.

Not in-sample and lightly multiple-tested: 6 models with one configuration each and no tuning. However, the sealed 20% out-of-sample block was never scored (notebook summary). All figures come from walk-forward validation inside the development set.

claim: kNN analogs over 35 multiscale EURUSD state columns beat HAR by +0.042 correlation on the next-hour standardised log range (CI [0.037, 0.047]) but trail GBR by 0.0135. The neighbours carry volatility and time of day, not direction. No trading edge measured.
reasons: The numbers match their source files exactly. results/80_analog_knn.csv, pooled row (fold=-1, n_val=22,616): gbr 0.7008, knn_k100 0.6873, knn_k50 0.6859, har_ms 0.6457, persistence 0.6424, knn_k1 0.4620 (r2 -0.0700). knn_k100 minus har_ms is +0.04167 [0.03689, 0.04654]; knn_k100 minus gbr is -0.01348 [-0.01645, -0.01050]. Per fold, knn_k100 beats har_ms and loses to gbr in all 6 folds: fold 1 0.6522/0.6262/0.6661 ... fold 6 0.7061/0.6545/0.7213. The notebook's other figures (contrast 10.09 vs 1.22, participation ratio 8.25, 14 components for 90% of variance, Leiden 0.7545 vs 0.3261, +0.004 distance-error correlation) are stored cell outputs. I could not re-run them without executing the notebook, which was off limits.

The features show no look-ahead. multiscale.py:114-118 and :243-287 build every feature from trailing windows with min_samples equal to the window. The target is the forward window (t, t+h] (multiscale.py:290-306). Corpus rows are cut at ts+60m <= knowable_by (vectors.py:280-283). Validation starts purge = 14,400+4,320 = 18,720 rows (about 13 trading days) after train_stop (split.py:74; vector_store.py:293). Corpora and baselines sit on a 60-minute stride and queries are hourly, so each target window is disjoint from the next.

Minor defect in the label. The comment at multiscale.py:299-300 says the target is standardised by statistics ending at t. The code at :302-306 computes (trail - mu)/sd and only then applies .shift(-horizon), so mu and sd end at t+60. The normaliser therefore contains the 60 forward rows (60 of 14,400, about 0.4%). Every model is scored on the same target, so the comparisons are unaffected. It should be fixed before any production label is built from it.

This is walk-forward out-of-sample within the development region (2020-09 to about 2024-09) only. The 20% sealed holdout (split.dev_oos_split, 0.80) was never scored. Separately, the illustration in cell 16 draws a query from 2025-07-16, inside the sealed region. That is a peek at the holdout, but it feeds no score.

Multiple testing is small. Six k values were swept (vector_store.py:63) and k=100 was chosen after the fact on the same validation rows. The curve is flat from k=50 to k=400 (0.6859 to 0.6873 to 0.6841), so the selection bias is at most about 0.003. The bootstrap block is 120 hourly rows, about one week (vector_store.py:328). The repo's own measured volatility memory is 8-17 trading days, so the intervals are probably somewhat too narrow. Still, a 6/6 fold sign agreement and a delta 8x its half-width survive that.

The +0.042 over HAR partly reflects a weak baseline. har_ms is OLS on three z-scored rv rungs with no intraday seasonality (vector_store.py:113-114). kNN over 35 columns picks up time of day implicitly: the Leiden communities split by hour, and the ms_span_* columns encode session breaks. GBR on the same columns gets more, so retrieval adds nothing over the fitted model.

There is no trading edge, and costs cannot be applied. The target is a standardised volatility magnitude with no direction (the notebook's own cell 18 says so, and 06_candle_direction puts EURUSD direction at chance). No P&L, win rate or payoff ratio is computed, so the MNQ round trip of 1.39 points has nothing to erase. The instrument is EURUSD, not MNQ.

Nothing here can be reproduced from the lake. The input bars are read from the curated forex parquet (data.py:4-5, 57), which CLAUDE.md classes as staging rather than a source. The store is a local file (Trading/forexmodel/data/vectors/eurusd.duckdb), the results are local CSVs, and none of it is landed: a dashboard information_schema query for vector/analog/forex tables returned [].
usable_for_design: This can be used only as a volatility/regime input, never as a direction signal. What can be carried over: (1) GBR on the 35 multiscale columns forecasts next-hour standardised range at corr 0.70 walk-forward (dev region only). That is useful for sizing stops and targets or for a volatility gate on a 2:1 payoff design. (2) kNN retrieval is dominated by GBR (-0.0135, 6/6 folds), so a vector store adds cost without accuracy. Its one open use is as an ensemble member whose errors may differ from GBR's, which was not measured. (3) Mean neighbour distance is not a confidence signal (+0.004 correlation with absolute error). (4) Engineering rule: filter the HNSW corpus when it is written, never with WHERE at query time. Before relying on any of it: fix the target normaliser so it ends at t, score once on the sealed 20% holdout, land the results in the lake, and add an intraday-seasonality HAR baseline. Nothing in the notebook shows EURUSD evidence for a 40% win rate or a 2:1 payoff, and it has no MNQ evidence at all.

claim: HAR+clock predicts next-hour log realized variance of MNQ 5-minute RTH returns out of sample (R2 +0.52, corr 0.69, 27/27 folds positive); direction has no skill; this is a risk forecast, not a trading edge.
reasons: Reproduces exactly from the lake. I pulled MNQZ5 1m bars from `bars` (true UTC; lean/scripts/lake_bars.py reads `bars`, not the Pacific-stamped `ohlcv` snapshot), clipped them to 09:30-17:00 ET, built 5m bars and re-ran the notebook's own walk-forward (cells 13/17 logic: 1200 train / 11 purge / 120 test). Result: HAR+clock R2 +0.5226, corr +0.6938, 27/27 folds positive, worst fold +0.074, n=3,240. That matches the auditor and the notebook. Script: scratchpad wf.py.

I found no look-ahead. Features at row t use returns up to and including bar t's close (trailing, min_periods == window, cell 9:202-211). The label uses bars t+1..t+12 within the same session (cell 13:300-325). The purge of 11 rows means the first test label begins at least 13 bars after the last training label, and dropped rows only widen that gap. The clock factor is fitted on bars [0, last train bar] in every fold (cell 17:494). The full-sample clock leak is worth +0.011, which confirms the guard.

The headline number is the best of the six quarters I tested (selection effect). HAR+clock pooled out-of-sample R2 by quarter's front contract: MNQZ5 Q4-2025 +0.523; MNQH5 +0.485; MNQM5 +0.431; MNQZ4 +0.346; MNQU5 +0.250; MNQH4 +0.239. The median across the six is about +0.39. Correlation runs 0.486-0.710.

'All 27 folds positive' does not hold in the other quarters. Positive folds: MNQU5 22/28 (worst -0.42), MNQM5 26/31 (worst -0.48), MNQH5 25/26 (worst -0.55), MNQZ4 25/28 (worst -0.41), MNQH4 24/27 (worst -0.36). The folds are adjacent 10-hour blocks with persistent volatility, so fold counts are not independent evidence.

The baseline is weak. R2 is measured against the rolling 1,200-row training mean, so a volatility-level shift between the training and test windows counts as skill. A no-fit persistence forecast (next hour's log variance = last hour's) scores +0.40 on MNQZ5 but only +0.05 to +0.32 in the other quarters. Most of the skill is last-hour persistence, which is a textbook stylized fact rather than a discovery.

'HAR+clock beats HAR' has the same sign in all 6 quarters (+0.04 to +0.08 R2). That partly answers the notebook's own worry that the top two rungs are inseparable (cell 26). The per-quarter separation is still untested: I did not run the block-bootstrap or Giacomini-White/Clark-West cells.

Costs cannot erase it, and cannot be applied to it: nothing is traded. The notebook's stated use, gating bars whose expected move cannot clear 0.554 bp, would almost never fire. The mean absolute next-hour move is 14-34 bp in every quarter (SQL over the same 5m RTH bars), so the round trip is roughly 2-4% of a typical hourly move.
Direction (R2 -0.02, sign accuracy 0.47) was not re-tested here. It matches the notebook's cell 25 by the auditor's run, and it is consistent with no directional edge.

Multiple testing is small: 5 nested rungs and one horizon/window configuration. The larger risk is the choice of quarter, shown above. The sample is 59 sessions of one expiry, about 270 non-overlapping hours per quarter.
corrected_numbers: HAR+clock walk-forward out-of-sample R2 on log next-hour variance (MNQ 5m, 09:30-17:00 ET, the notebook's scheme, bars from the lake `bars` view): MNQZ5 Q4-25 +0.523 (corr 0.694, 27/27 folds positive); MNQH5 +0.485 (0.704, 25/26); MNQM5 +0.431 (0.710, 26/31); MNQZ4 +0.346 (0.587, 25/28); MNQU5 +0.250 (0.489, 22/28); MNQH4 +0.239 (0.486, 24/27). Six-quarter median about +0.39, range 0.24-0.52. Over the same folds, 1h-variance-only R2: 0.21-0.48. Clock-only R2: 0.04-0.14. No-fit persistence R2: 0.05-0.40. Mean absolute next-hour move: 14-34 bp vs a 0.554 bp round trip.
usable_for_design: Usable as a volatility input, not as a return signal. A trailing HAR (12/84/252-bar realized variance) plus a clock factor fitted on training rows only gives a causal next-hour variance forecast with honest out-of-sample R2 of about 0.24-0.52 across six MNQ quarters. Plan on about +0.35-0.40, not +0.52. Use it for position sizing, volatility-scaled stop and target distances (relevant to a 2:1 reward/risk design), and regime features for a direction model. It supplies no win rate or expectancy by itself. Any P&L claim built on it needs its own cost-inclusive walk-forward backtest. Its 0.554 bp cost gate is not a meaningful filter at this horizon.
